headline: High: Cursor’s broad filesystem, shell, network, and MCP access can amplify shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage when paired with marketingskills’ shared-context skills files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests files, clipboard, and MCP outputs by default, and marketingskills explicitly uses shared-context skill files that reference each other. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if untrusted content lands in the shared workspace. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF untrusted text is placed in workspace files or skill files that Cursor reads
IF marketingskills skill references are edited by a lower-trust process
mitigations: Separate the two agents into different workspaces
Disable or restrict MCP servers in Cursor
Review shared skill files before opening them in Cursor
Use read-only copies for marketingskills inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared-context files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write local files, and Cursor touches open files, clipboard contents, and sends data to model providers. marketingskills stores marketing context in local skill files. Shared workspace plus outbound inference creates a realistic leakage path for sensitive content, though the data classes are not inherently high sensitivity.
conditions: IF sensitive marketing context is stored in the shared workspace
IF Cursor is allowed to send those files to external model providers
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Turn off clipboard sharing between tools
Use local-only models for sensitive sessions
Restrict Cursor to a dedicated project folder
requires-engineering: enforce per-file egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted local write, shell, and git modification capability, while marketingskills also writes files and reads the filesystem. Because Cursor’s shared state is via local filesystem, concurrent edits can collide on shared files or generated skill artifacts. No locking is documented, so conflict risk exists in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or skill directory
IF concurrent writes occur without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Place marketingskills in a separate checkout
Pause Cursor auto-runs during skill generation
Use git branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code or edits from its agent loop, and marketingskills explicitly builds on shared context across skills. If Cursor-produced content is treated as authoritative by the skill system, errors can cascade into reused marketing artifacts. The pair lacks documented verification boundaries, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Cursor-generated text is copied into marketingskills skill files
IF marketingskills reuses that text without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before promoting generated text
Mark generated snippets clearly in filenames
Keep source notes separate from reusable skills
Use a checklist for factual claims
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles model-provider API keys and broad workspace content, while marketingskills is a marketing-content skill set with local files and no stated regulated-data handling. The main compliance issue is policy mismatch or accidental retention, not a documented residency or certification breach. Only Cursor is directly relevant here; marketingskills is cited to show the shared content class.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is placed into marketing skill files
IF Cursor’s provider retention settings are not configured for that data class
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared marketing files
Review provider retention settings in Cursor
Store compliance-sensitive content outside the pair
Add a short data-class label to each workspace
requires-engineering: formalize retention and residency controls
